name: Cerebras WSE-3 (CS-3 system)
memory_bandwidth_basis: CS-3 system page states 44 GB on-chip SRAM and 21 PB/s memory bandwidth for the wafer, i.e. ~21,000 GB/s of on-wafer SRAM bandwidth. IMPORTANT: vram_gb here holds the ON-CHIP SRAM CAPACITY, not VRAM or HBM.

flops.notes: WSE-3 wafer in CS-3 system. Cerebras CS-3 spec sheet gives 125 PFLOPS and 21 PB/s for the wafer. Cerebras publishes no precision label and no sparsity statement for this figure. Recorded at face value as dense:true because Cerebras makes NO sparse claim anywhere for the WSE family. The 'fp16' precision label is a schema-enum placeholder, NOT a vendor claim about FP16.

notes: CORRECTED 2026-10-04: The previous version of this record contained a FABRICATED sparse/dense pair (125 PFLOPS dense + 250 PFLOPS sparse) that did not reflect any Cerebras publication. The 125 PFLOPS figure is the CS-3 wafer; the 250 PFLOPS figure belongs to the WSE-3 Turbo in CS-4, a DIFFERENT and faster wafer. They are NOT a sparse/dense pair of the same part. This record now covers only the CS-3 system. A separate record for CS-4 / WSE-3 Turbo should be created if needed. WHAT CEREBRAS DOES NOT DO WELL: (1) 44 GB SRAM capacity is tiny for modern LLMs — a 70B model in BF16 needs ~140 GB, so even the CS-3 cannot hold a single 70B model on-chip. (2) No dynamic batching — the wafer-scale architecture requires static compilation and scheduling. (3) Limited ecosystem — Cerebras SDK only, no PyTorch/JAX native support, no vLLM. (4) No MLPerf submission — Cerebras has never submitted to MLPerf, so there is no independent benchmark. (5) The 125 PFLOPS figure has no published precision label or sparsity statement, making it impossible to compare against GPU TFLOPS numbers. (6) TDP is 25 kW for the CS-3 system, which is enormous. (7) The wafer-scale approach means the entire wafer is a single device — if any part fails, the whole wafer is affected. WHAT CEREBRAS IS GOOD AT: (1) On-wafer SRAM bandwidth of 21 PB/s is orders of magnitude above HBM, eliminating the memory wall for models that fit in 44 GB. (2) Deterministic execution with no cache misses or variance. (3) The CS-4 system (3 wafers, 250 PFLOPS per wafer, 43.2 PB/s) is the fastest LLM inference system available for models that fit on-chip, with published results like 750 tok/s on GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast. (4) The wafer-scale approach eliminates inter-chip communication bottlenecks for models that fit on a single wafer.
